newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks edge down on light profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks edge down on light profit-taking.

text.p: Mexican stocks inched down at the open on Thursday in what traders said was light profit-taking amid market uncertainty over whether shares could continue their recent bull run, traders said.
"It's very quiet, no one wants to settle deals, they don't know which way it will go, although profit-taking is more than overdue," a desk trader said.
The leading IPC share index was down 4.44 points in the opening minutes of trade, or 0.09 percent, at 4,832.05. Trading volume was light at 2.6 million shares.
Traders noted that blue chips were leading the slide.
"Blue chips are weighing the market down, there's some selling to offset the window-dressing we saw at the close yesterday," a floor trader said. "Telmex is the only prop."
Financial firm Bancomer and maize flour maker Maseca were the most heavily traded sliders.
Bancomer had trimmed 1 centavo from its recent gains to 4.49 pesos, while Maseca had shed 4 centavos to 9.30 pesos.
Market heavyweight Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) was meanwhile up 10 centavos to 21.00 pesos.
Dealers said Telmex was one of the few blue chips to benefit from early gains on Wall Street, where its ADRs had advanced 1/16 to 53-3/8.
The Dow Jones industrial average had meanwhile gained 30.99 points to 7,873.42.
The broad market matched the downward trend among blue chips. Decliners outweighed gainers by 16 to 11, out of 37 stocks that had changed hands.
